definition: Stacking semiconductor layers with progressively lower band gaps reduces the energy wasted as heat and raises overall conversion efficiency versus a single-layer cell.
core_idea: A single band gap wastes energy from photons that are either below threshold (unabsorbed) or well above it (excess becomes heat); layering high-to-low band-gap materials lets more of the solar spectrum be captured usefully.
key_points: First layer uses a high band-gap material, followed by progressively lower band-gap layers.
This staged approach is presented as a way to improve on the low efficiency of a simple single-layer solar cell.
relationships: Directly addresses the inefficiency mechanism described in the basic PV effect.
